Proposition
[zero sets of commuting Killing fields]

Source: petersen:page-0341 ↗ def:pet-ch8-killing-field ↗ prop:pet-ch8-killing-curvature-identities 1. ch8:8.3.8Let $(M,g)$ be compact and $X,Y\in \iso (M,g)$ commute.

  1. $Y$ is tangent to the level sets of $|X|^2$, in particular to the zero set of $X$.

  2. If $X$ and $Y$ both vanish on a totally geodesic submanifold $N\subset M$, then some linear combination of $X,Y$ vanishes on a strictly larger connected submanifold.

Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch8-commuting-killing-fields-properties \sketch Since $[X,Y]=0$, invariance of both $g$ and $X$ under the $Y$-flow gives $D_Y|X|^2=0$, proving the first assertion. At $p\in N$, section 1 gives $[( abla X)_p,( abla Y)_p]=0$. These commuting skew-adjoint maps split the normal space of $N$ into common invariant $2$-planes, while section 1 identifies $T_pN$ with their common kernel. On one normal block a nonzero linear combination of the two maps vanishes. The corresponding combination of $X,Y$ therefore has a zero component whose tangent space strictly contains $T_pN$.

□
